title: A family’s AI-assisted fertility story shows both value and danger in persistent questioning
friendlyTitle: One family used AI to ask better fertility questions—but it also made mistakes
summary: In a guest essay, Drew Housman recounts using ChatGPT to explore questions during years of infertility treatment; a suggestion to discuss an MRI with clinicians led to the discovery of a fibroid. The account also describes false statements from the model and is one family’s experience, not clinical evidence that a chatbot can diagnose safely.
friendlySummary: A family says ChatGPT suggested a question that helped doctors find a fibroid after years of treatment. The chatbot also gave wrong answers, and this is one personal story.
whyItMatters: AI can help patients prepare questions and navigate limited appointment time, but a compelling success story can hide false positives, unnecessary testing and unequal access. Use it to organize concerns and ask a qualified clinician, not to interpret a scan or make a medical decision on its own.
friendlyWhyItMatters: AI can help you prepare questions for a doctor. Do not let it diagnose you or make an important health decision by itself.
